mechanisms.material_state: T6 (solution treated, quenched, pre-deformed and aged) pre-deformed

evidence.quote: The higher strength of the pre-deformed alloy could be related to the higher density of the precipitates, which grow on the twin boundaries and can hinder the dislocation movement and strengthen the alloy.

mechanisms.name: dislocation hindering by precipitates
mechanisms.material_state: T6 (solution treated, quenched, pre-deformed and aged) pre-deformed

evidence.quote: the precipitates, which grow on the twin boundaries and can hinder the dislocation movement and strengthen the alloy

By increasing the volume fraction and aspect ratio of the precipitates, the strengthening effect will be greater [22]. The improvement of the strength by thermo-mechanical process can be attributed to the higher volume fraction of the β′ precipitates in the pre-deformed samples (Figure 6).
It seems that twin-induced hardening is particularly potent in the pre-deformed samples.
the pre-deformed alloy shows a higher number of multiple slips, helping explain the higher strength of the pre-deformed alloy at this test temperature
at higher test temperatures activation of the non-basal slips increases the ductility of magnesium alloys [21]
Improvement of the high temperature strength of the alloy was related to the solution strengthening of rare earth elements and precipitation of β′ phases on the prismatic plane.
